spots.name: Clifton Suspension Bridge
spots.summary: The Clifton Suspension Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Avon Gorge and the River Avon, linking Clifton in Bristol to Leigh Woods in North Somerset. Since opening in 1864, it has been a toll bridge, the income from which provides funds for its maintenance.

spots.name: SS Great Britain

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: SS Great Britain is a museum ship and former passenger steamship that was advanced for her time. The largest passenger ship in the world from 1845 to 1853, she was designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel (1806–1859), for the Great Western Steamship Company's transatlantic service between Bristol and New York City.

spots.name: Bristol Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bristol Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of the Holy and Undivided Trinity, is a Church of England cathedral in the city of Bristol, England. It is the seat of the Bishop of Bristol. The cathedral was originally an abbey dedicated to St Augustine, founded in 1140 and consecrated in 1148.

spots.name: Bristol Temple Meads railway station
spots.summary: Bristol Temple Meads is the oldest and largest railway station in Bristol, England. It is located 118 miles 31 chains away from London Paddington.

spots.name: Matthew

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Matthew was a caravel sailed by John Cabot in 1497 from Bristol to Newfoundland, North America. There are two modern replicas – one in Bristol, England and one in Bonavista, Newfoundland.

spots.name: Pero's Bridge
spots.summary: Pero's Bridge is a pedestrian bascule bridge that spans St Augustine's Reach in Bristol Harbour, Bristol, England. It links Queen Square and Millennium Square.

photo.author: The original uploader was Rodw at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: St Mary Redcliffe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St Mary the Virgin, widely known as St Mary Redcliffe, is the main Church of England parish church for the Redcliffe district of the city of Bristol, England. The first reference to a church on the site appears in 1158, with the present building dating from 1185 to 1872.

photo.author: Matt Gibson from Bristol, United Kingdom

spots.name: Clifton Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of SS. Peter and Paul is the Roman Catholic cathedral of the city of Bristol. Located in the Clifton area of the city, it is the seat and mother church of the Diocese of Clifton and is known as Clifton Cathedral. It has been a Grade II* Listed Building since 2000.

photo.author: The original uploader was Rbrwr at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Bristol Zoo
spots.summary: Bristol Zoo Gardens was a zoo in the city of Bristol in South West England. Bristol Zoo Gardens was managed by the education and conservation charity Bristol Zoological Society, which also manages Bristol Zoo Project.

spots.name: Bristol Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bristol Castle was a Norman castle established in the late 11th century on the north bank of the River Avon in Bristol. Remains can be seen today in Castle Park near the Broadmead Shopping Centre, including the sally port.

photo.author: The book's text by JF Nicholls (d. 1883) and John Taylor (d. 1893). Death dates

spots.name: Clifton College
spots.summary: Clifton College is a public school in the city of Bristol in South West England, founded in 1862 and offering both boarding and day school for pupils aged 13–18.

spots.name: Arnolfini

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Arnolfini is an international arts centre and gallery in Bristol, England. It has a programme of contemporary art exhibitions, artist's performance, music and dance events, poetry and book readings, talks, lectures and cinema. There is also a specialist art bookshop and a café bar.

spots.name: Bristol Old Vic
spots.summary: Bristol Old Vic is a British theatre company based at the Theatre Royal, Bristol. The present company was established in 1946 as an offshoot of the Old Vic in London. It is associated with the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, which became a financially independent organisation in the 1990s.

photo.author: The original uploader was Rbrwr at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Bristol Museum & Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Bristol Museum & Art Gallery is a large museum and art gallery in Bristol, England. The museum is situated in Clifton, about 0.5 miles (0.8 km) from the city centre. As part of Bristol Culture and Creative Industries it is run by Bristol City Council with no entrance fee.

photo.author: The original uploader was Steinsky at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: M Shed

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: M Shed is a museum in Bristol, England, located on Prince's Wharf beside the Floating Harbour in a dockside transit shed formerly occupied by Bristol Industrial Museum. The museum's name is derived from the way that the port identified each of its sheds.

spots.name: Bristol Hippodrome
spots.summary: The Bristol Hippodrome is a theatre located in The Centre, Bristol, England, United Kingdom with seating on three levels giving a capacity of 1,951. It frequently features shows from London's West End when they tour the UK, as well as regular visits by Welsh National Opera and an annual pantomime.

spots.name: Bristol Bridge
spots.summary: Bristol Bridge is a bridge over the floating harbour in Bristol, England. The floating harbour was constructed on the original course of the River Avon, and there has been a bridge on the site since long before the harbour was created by impounding the river in 1809.

spots.name: Cabot Tower
spots.summary: Cabot Tower is a tower in Bristol, England, situated in a public park on Brandon Hill, between the city centre, Clifton and Hotwells. It is a grade II listed building.

spots.name: Wills Memorial Building
spots.summary: The Wills Memorial Building is a neo-Gothic building in Bristol, England, designed by Sir George Oatley and built as a memorial to Henry Overton Wills III by his sons George and Henry Wills. Begun in 1915 and not opened until 1925, it is considered one of the last great Gothic buildings to be built in England.

spots.name: Llandoger Trow
spots.summary: The Llandoger Trow is a historic public house in Bristol, England. Dating from 1664, it is on King Street, between Welsh Back and Queen Charlotte Street, near the old city centre docks.

spots.name: Queen Square
spots.summary: Queen Square is a 2.4 hectares Georgian square in the centre of Bristol, England. Following the 1831 riot, Queen Square declined through the latter part of the 19th century, was threatened with a main line railway station, but then bisected by a dual carriageway in the 1930s.

spots.name: Clifton Observatory
spots.summary: Clifton Observatory is a former mill, now used as an observatory, located on Clifton Down, close to the Clifton Suspension Bridge in Bristol, England.

spots.name: Christmas Steps
spots.summary: Christmas Steps is a historic street in the city centre of Bristol, England.

spots.name: Stokes Croft
spots.summary: Stokes Croft is a road in Bristol, England. It is part of the A38, a main road north of the city centre. Locals refer to the area around the road by the same name.

spots.name: Temple Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Temple Church, also known as Holy Cross Church, is a ruined church in Redcliffe, Bristol, England. It is on the site of a previous, round church of the Knights Templar, which they built on land granted to them in the second quarter of the 12th century by Robert of Gloucester.

spots.name: All Saints' Church, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: All Saints is a closed Anglican church in Corn Street, Bristol. For many years it was used as a Diocesan Education Centre, but this closed in 2015. The building has been designated as a grade II* listed building.

spots.name: Underfall Yard
spots.summary: The Underfall Yard is a historic boatyard on Spike Island serving Bristol Harbour in England.

spots.name: St Stephen's Church, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Stephen's Church in St Stephen's Avenue, is the parish church for the city of Bristol, England.

spots.name: St Mary le Port Church, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Mary le Port is a ruined parish church in the centre of Bristol, England, situated in Castle Park on what remains of Mary le Port Street.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Mary le Port Church, Bristol

spots.name: A Surge of Power (Jen Reid) 2020
spots.summary: A Surge of Power 2020 is a 2020 black resin sculpture, sculpted by Marc Quinn and modelled on Jen Reid; both Quinn and Reid are credited as artists. It depicts Reid, a black female protester, raising her arm in a Black Power salute.

spots.name: We The Curious

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: We The Curious is a science and arts centre and educational charity in Bristol, England. It has over 200 interactive exhibits, is home to the UK’s first 3D Planetarium and hosts over 300,000 visitors a year.

spots.name: College Green
spots.summary: College Green is a public open space in Bristol, England. The Green takes the form of a segment of a circle with its apex pointing east, and covers 1.1 hectares.

spots.name: Castle Park, Bristol
spots.summary: Castle Park is a public open space in Bristol, England, managed by Bristol City Council. It is bounded by the Floating Harbour and Castle Street to the south, Lower Castle Street to the east, and Broad Weir, Newgate and Wine Street to the north.

spots.name: Corn Street
spots.summary: Corn Street, together with Broad Street, Wine Street and High Street, is one of the four cross streets which met at the Bristol High Cross, the heart of Bristol, England when it was a walled medieval town.

spots.name: Church of St John the Baptist, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St John the Baptist in Bristol, also known as St John on the Wall, is a historic church in the care of heritage charity the Churches Conservation Trust. The upper church and its medieval vaulted crypt is located at the lower end of Broad Street and is built into the old city's medieval walls.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St John the Baptist, Bristol

spots.name: Broadmead
spots.summary: Broadmead is a street in Bristol city centre in England, which has given its name to the principal shopping district of the city. It is part of Bristol Shopping Quarter.

spots.name: The Exchange
spots.summary: The Exchange is a Grade I listed building built in 1741–43 by John Wood the Elder, on Corn Street, near the junction with Broad Street in Bristol, England. It was previously used as a corn and general trade exchange but is now used as offices and it also accommodates St Nicholas Market.

spots.name: St Nicholas, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Nicholas is a church in St Nicholas Street, Bristol, England. The church was bombed in the Second World War and rebuilt in 1974–1975 as a church museum.

spots.name: St Peter's Church, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Peter's Church is a ruined church in Castle Park, Bristol, England. It was bombed during World War II and is now preserved as a memorial.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Peter's Church, Castle Park, Bristol

spots.name: Everard's Printing Works
spots.summary: The Former Everard's Printing Works is at 37–38 Broad Street in Bristol, England. It has been designated as a Grade II* listed building.

spots.name: Bristol Beacon
spots.summary: Bristol Beacon, previously Colston Hall, is a concert hall and Grade II listed building on Colston Street, Bristol, England. It is owned by Bristol City Council. Since 2011, it has been managed by Bristol Music Trust.

spots.name: King Street
spots.summary: King Street is a 17th-century street in the historic city centre of Bristol, England.

spots.name: Redcliffe Shot Tower
spots.summary: The Redcliffe Shot Tower was a historic shot tower in the English city of Bristol. It was the progenitor of many similar towers built around the world. The tower stood at the corner of Redcliffe Hill and Redcliffe Parade, in the suburb of Redcliffe, between the years of 1782 and 1968.

spots.name: Cheese Lane Shot Tower
spots.summary: The Cheese Lane Shot Tower is a grade II listed shot tower in the English city of Bristol. It was built in 1969, and was a replacement for an earlier shot tower, the very first such tower ever built.

spots.name: Gromit Unleashed
spots.summary: Gromit Unleashed was a public charity art trail led by Wallace & Gromit's Grand Appeal and Aardman Animations, in which 80 giant artist-decorated fibreglass sculptures of Gromit were displayed on the streets of Bristol and the surrounding area between 1 July and 8 September 2013.

spots.name: St James' Priory, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Priory Church of St James, Bristol, is a Grade I listed building in Horsefair, Whitson Street.

spots.name: Millennium Square
spots.summary: Millennium Square is a city square in the Canon's Marsh area of Bristol, England. It was built in the late 1990s as part of the harbourside regeneration and We The Curious development, and has become a popular public area and event space.

spots.name: Royal West of England Academy

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal West of England Academy (RWA) is Bristol's oldest art gallery, located in Clifton, Bristol, near the junction of Queens Road and Whiteladies Road. Situated in a Grade II* listed building, it hosts five galleries and an exhibition programme of historic and contemporary British art.

spots.name: St Mark's Church, Bristol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Mark's Church is an ancient church on the north-east side of College Green, Bristol, England, built c. 1230. Better known to mediaeval and Tudor historians as the Gaunt's Chapel, it has also been known within Bristol since 1722 as the Lord Mayor's Chapel.

spots.name: Commercial Rooms, Bristol
spots.summary: The Commercial Rooms are on Corn Street in Bristol, England.

spots.name: St Nicholas Market

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: St Nicholas Market is a market in The Exchange on Corn Street in Bristol, England. It is also home to the Bristol Farmers' Market, the Nails Market, and the Slow Food Market, all of which are located in front of the Exchange.

spots.name: Statue of Edmund Burke
spots.summary: The statue of Edmund Burke in Bristol, England, is a commemorative bronze sculpture of Edmund Burke (1729–1797) standing in The Centre. It was created in 1894 by James Havard Thomas and is grade II listed.

spots.name: St Michael on the Mount Without

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mount Without, formerly the Church of St Michael on the Mount Without, is a former church, now a creative space, on St Michael's Hill in Kingsdown, Bristol, England, near the University of Bristol.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Michael on the Mount Without

spots.name: Ashton Court

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ashton Court is a mansion house and estate to the west of Bristol in England. Although the estate lies mainly in North Somerset, it is owned by the City of Bristol. The mansion and stables are a Grade I listed building. Other structures on the estate are also listed.

spots.name: St Mary on the Quay

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Mary on the Quay is a Roman Catholic Parish church in Bristol, England. It is situated on Colston Avenue, next to Beacon Tower in the centre of the city. It is the oldest Roman Catholic church in Bristol; the first one built after the Reformation.

spots.name: Park Street
spots.summary: Park Street is a major shopping street in Bristol, England, linking the city centre to Clifton. It forms part of the A4018.

spots.name: Bristol Cathedral Choir School

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bristol Cathedral Choir School is a mixed gender non-selective musical secondary school with academy status, in the Cabot area of Bristol, England. Until 2008 it was Bristol Cathedral School, part of Bristol Cathedral, in the centre of the city.

spots.name: equestrian statue of William III
spots.summary: The equestrian statue of William III is a historic statue in the centre of Queen Square in Bristol, England. It is a Grade I listed building.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Equestrian statue of William III, Bristol

spots.name: Red Lodge Museum, Bristol

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Red Lodge Museum is a historic house museum in Bristol, England. The original building was Tudor/Elizabethan, and construction began in 1579–1580, possibly to the design of Sebastiano Serlio. The main additional building phases are from the 1730s and the early 19th century.

spots.name: Aerospace Bristol
spots.summary: Aerospace Bristol is an aerospace museum at Filton, to the north of Bristol, England. The project is run by the Bristol Aero Collection Trust and houses a varied collection of exhibits, including Concorde Alpha Foxtrot, the final Concorde to be built and the last to fly.

spots.name: Bristol Blue Glass
spots.summary: Glass workshop producing traditional blue glass, a local specialty since the late 18th century. Cobalt oxide and lead oxide are mixed into the molten glass, giving it its characteristic deep blue colour. The glass workshop can be visited on request with a tour along the furnaces. It also includes a shop where glassware can be purchased.

spots.name: Hengrove Park Leisure Centre

hours.note: Closed Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun

spots.summary: Gym, Olympic swimming pool, 4 court sports hall, dance studio, health suite, and an 8-m climbing wall to the south of Bristol.
